messages:
maya: Hey team — customer on prod is seeing repeated tool-call failures when we stream the tool args. They send a streaming completion with function call but the args arrive as a partial JSON and the tool rejects it. Here's the repro and sample.

alex: Thanks — can you paste the raw SSE/chunked body they received? small example is enough.

maya: Pasting obfuscated log from the edge (newlines preserved):

--- HTTP response body (chunked) ---
1f
{
  "name": "createOrder",
  "args": {
    "order_id": "ord_12345",
    "items": [
      {"sku": "S-001", "qty": 2},
      {"sku": "S-002", "qty": 1}
    ],
    "total": 42.5
  }
}

10
}

--- end ---

maya: Notice second chunk is just a trailing brace '}' on its own, but some customers see the stream cut off in the middle of the args, e.g. they get '\"items\": [\n      {\"sku\": \"S-001\", \"qty\": 2},\n      {\"sku\": \"S-002\",' and then connection close. Tool layer complains: "unexpected end of JSON input".

ingrid: Are they using our hosted API or Dedicated/private? Could be proxy buffer sizing or an upstream LB dropping mid-chunk.

maya: Hosted API. Customer is in eu-west and hitting our public endpoint. They've tried twice with different client libs (node-fetch and python requests) and both showed the truncated tail in their client-side capture.

alex: Two quick theories: 1) our reverse-proxy (nginx) is buffering and splitting multibyte UTF-8 sequences across chunks leading to corruption on reassembly; 2) some intermediate CDN/edge is doing premature connection close at idle windows. Do we have the full server-side logs for that request-id?

maya: Request id: rqc_9b8f2f. Attached server logs (excerpt):

[2026-02-14T09:32:45Z] rqc_9b8f2f stream start, model=gpt-*-toolcall, routing=eu-west-1
[2026-02-14T09:32:46Z] rqc_9b8f2f upstream write n=512
[2026-02-14T09:32:46Z] rqc_9b8f2f upstream write n=32
[2026-02-14T09:32:47Z] rqc_9b8f2f connection reset by peer (read: connection timed out)

sre_oncall: The writes look like the runtime flushed two writes (512 bytes then 32 bytes). Reset by peer indicates remote side closed the socket before completing the stream. Could be the client or an intermediary. Any proxy headers from the customer capture? e.g., Via or X-Forwarded-For chain.

maya: Customer sent their capture with headers: Via: 1.1 edge-cdn; X-Accel-Buffering: no; Transfer-Encoding: chunked; Content-Encoding: gzip (they gzip the request body). They said turning off gzip on the client made the issue rare but still happened.

alex: gzip + chunked can be tricky if a proxy ungzips/inspects and then re-chunks. Also if chunk boundaries split gzip block sequences the downstream might not reassemble correctly. Does our ingress ever do streaming gzip inspection? Ingrid?

ingrid: Our ingress does not decompress request bodies by default, but the CDN might. I'll open a ticket with infra to check edge CDN behavior for gzipped chunked uploads. For immediate triage: can the customer try sending args base64-encoded as a single token string so we avoid special chars/newlines and gzipping? That will at least tell us if chunk boundary splitting is the root cause.

maya: I asked them to test base64 encode — they said encoded payloads completed successfully twice in a row. Also they tried forcing Connection: close on the client and saw fewer truncations.

sre_oncall: That lines up with edge reusing keep-alive connections and an aggressive idle timeout. Action items: 1) infra to look up CDN idle/timeout and gzip passthrough; 2) SDK team to add a mitigation note for streaming tool args (base64 or single-line minified JSON) and a retry wrapper for partial JSON parse errors; 3) support to provide workaround to the customer and monitor.

support_bot: Ticket INC-4521 created for rqc_9b8f2f with severity P2. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.example/browse/INC-4521 :white_check_mark:

alex: For repro we should create a small harness that streams a gzipped chunked JSON where we intentionally split inside a UTF-8 multibyte sequence and then close the connection early. I'll put a quick node script in eng-repro and try to run against staging CDN to reproduce.

ingrid: Also add a test in runtime where we emit smaller intermediate flush sizes (imitate 128B/32B) to see if any internal layer mishandles reassembly.

maya: Customer accepted base64 workaround for now and asked for ETA on permanent fix. I'll keep them updated. I'll post updates to the ticket and link any infra findings here.

-- end thread --
